items.q: The inherited form of 11β-OH steroid dehydrogenase type 2 defect is called:
items.exp: Inherited 11β-HSD2 defect = apparent mineralocorticoid excess (AME). (Book p840)
The enzyme converts cortisol (glucocorticoid + mineralocorticoid) to cortisone (glucocorticoid only). (Book p840)

items.q: ‘In AME the blocked cortisol→cortisone step causes excess cortisol, which then acts as a mineralocorticoid.’
opts: True, but only with a tumour
items.exp: Blocking the conversion leaves excess cortisol driving mineralocorticoid effects (AME). (Book p840)

items.q: The acquired causes of 11β-HSD2 inhibition listed are:
items.exp: Acquired: Cushing's disease and licorice excess (inhibits 11β-OH steroid dehydrogenase type 2). (Book p840)

items.q: ‘Licorice excess produces hypertension by inhibiting 11β-OH steroid dehydrogenase type 2.’
items.exp: Licorice excess (−) inhibits 11β-HSD2, an acquired cause of the AME picture. (Book p840)

items.q: A child presents with hypertension, hypokalaemia and alkalosis with salt + water retention but low aldosterone. The shared presentation triangle points to:
items.exp: Both inherited and acquired 11β-HSD2 defects present with salt + H2O retention → HTN, alkalosis and hypokalaemia. (Book p840)

items.q: Which is NOT part of the presentation triangle of 11β-HSD2 defects?
items.exp: The triangle is hypertension, alkalosis and hypokalaemia (with salt + water retention); hyperkalaemia is the opposite. (Book p840)
